claims.assertion: The GPS record shows the actual driven distance was 8.5 km against an optimal route of 8.5 km, i.e. +0.0 km (-0%), so there is no off-route segment and no deviation to complain of; the driver did take the shortest and most direct route in distance terms.
The fare record independently confirms the billed distance 8.5 km does not exceed the optimal route distance (8.5 km), so no excess distance was billed and any RD-2 refund calculation returns zero.

The fare complaint cannot be met on the distance element: this is a RydeTAXI metered trip and the components charged - base $3.90, distance $11.99 for 8.50 km, time $5.72 for 22.0 min, waiting $0.00, platform $1.47, total $23.08 - contain no unbilled or unpublished extra item, and no surge applied (1.0x).

The higher-than-expected fare is explained by journey time and road conditions, not by routing: trip duration was 22.0 min against a 16.3 min estimate (+5.7 min), with heavy rain (18.5 mm, thundery showers) and recorded speed band 3 (20-29 km/h) on both PIE and Airport Boulevard across 17:09-17:47, and no traffic incidents near the route.
Because no off-route segment exists and no unpublished or non-compliant charge appears in the metered breakdown, the correct outcome for the fare dispute is no_action with the fare maintained.

A flag_account against the driver is not supported here: the driver's record shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so RD-6's repeated-violation condition is not met, and the rider's own record (0 disputes, 0 upheld) shows no pattern either.

Nothing in the record raises a safety event: there are no in-app chat messages (so no threats, harassment or dangerous-driving content) and the driver's post-trip statement only refers to following the app route, rain and slow traffic.

weaknesses: My own client's core premise is contradicted by the system records: F1 shows +0.0 km actual vs optimal and F3 shows billed distance 8.5 km = optimal, so the rider's belief that 'the driver must have taken a longer route' has no evidentiary basis and I cannot build a RD-2 refund on it.

The longer time component is visible in the fare and may still feel unfair to the rider: F2 (+5.7 min vs estimate) and F5 (time charge $5.72 for 22.0 min) are the real driver of the $23.08 total; the other side will cite F2, F8, F9 and F11 to say the delay was congestion and heavy rain, and RD-4 accepts traffic evidence, so a time-based grievance has no refund hook in the policy.
There is no chat consent to argue from either way: F6 records no in-app messages and F7 is a post-trip driver statement, so no RD-5 agreement (or its absence) can be established from the ride itself.

claims.assertion: There is no off-route segment in this trip: the GPS record shows actual distance 8.5 km against an optimal route of 8.5 km, +0.0 km (0%), so no RD-1 deviation exists to be exempted or refunded.

The billing record independently confirms no excess mileage: billed distance 8.5 km does not exceed the optimal route of 8.5 km, so the distance component of the metered fare is exactly what the shortest route would have produced.
Refund under RD-2 is therefore zero (0 km of unexempted extra_km × per-km rate = $0.00), and the correct disposition is no_action with no refund to compute.

The rider's 'longer route' theory is contradicted by the system records: the higher-than-expected fare is explained by time, not distance — duration was 22.0 min versus the 16.3 min estimate (+5.7 min), and the meter's time component is $5.72 of the $23.08 total.

The extra time is attributable to documented conditions outside the driver's control: heavy rain/thundery showers (18.5 mm) and speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on both the Pan Island Expressway and Airport Boulevard throughout 17:09–17:47, i.e. the whole trip window — consistent with the driver's statement that he followed the app route and traffic was slow.

No unexplained charge appears in the fare: surge multiplier is 1.0× and waiting is $0.00, and the total $23.08 is composed only of the metered base $3.90, distance $11.99, time $5.72 and the published platform fee $1.47 — nothing unpublished to strip out.

The rider has never had a dispute upheld (0 in 90 days) and the driver has no upheld route dispute in 90 days, so the RD-6 precondition for a flag_account (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met and no account flag is warranted.

weaknesses: The complaint mentions heavy rain, which the system also records (F11), and the trip took 5.7 minutes longer than estimated (F2) — the other side will argue the driver should have chosen a faster route; the answer is that no alternative-route record exists and RD-4(a) requires a traffic incident (F10 shows none), so no exemption/refund analysis arises.

RD-4(b) speed bands 3 on PIE and Airport Boulevard (F8, F9) are only corroborative and do not alone exempt a segment under RD-4; but since there is no off-route segment at all (F1, F3), this weakness is immaterial to the outcome.

The driver's statement (F7) that he 'followed the app route exactly' is uncorroborated driver testimony and cannot itself prove routing; we rely instead on the GPS and fare records (F1, F3), which the policy ranks above statements.

The fare is a metered RydeTAXI fare (F5), so any distance-based overcharge would be refundable — but the billed distance equals the optimal distance (F3), so the other side cannot point to any metre of chargeable detour.

This corroboration actually cuts against any complaint that the driver chose a needlessly slow route: F11 (heavy rain, 18.5 mm) and F8/F9 (speed band 3, 20-29 km/h on PIE and Airport Boulevard, 17:09-17:47) cover the whole 17:20-17:42 trip window while F10 records no incident, so the delay is environmental and no segment is chargeable under RD-4.

Accepted — billed distance 8.5 km does not exceed the 8.5 km optimal route, so the RD-2 formula yields zero unexempted extra_km and zero refund; this is the same conclusion my brief reached in D1–D3.

Accepted — the $23.08 metered breakdown contains only base $3.90, distance $11.99, time $5.72, waiting $0.00 and platform $1.47 at surge 1.0×, so there is no unpublished or non-compliant item to strip out under FARE-1.

Accepted and it supports my client: heavy rain (18.5 mm) plus speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) on PIE and Airport Boulevard over 17:09–17:47 explain the +5.7 min versus estimate, and RD-4 recognises such conditions on the optimal route; the delay is congestion and weather, not mileage.
